newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CA Currency Fund reaches 6.2 pct p.a. yield in H1.
newsitem.headline: CA Currency Fund reaches 6.2 pct p.a. yield in H1.

text.p: Hungary's Creditanstalt (CA) group said on Monday that it reached an annual 6.2 percent currency yield in the first half of the year through its CA Foreign Currency Bond Fund.
"The aim is to exceed yields of untied (foreign) currency deposits (by banks)," Csaba Lantos, director for fund management at Creditanstalt Securities, told a news conference.
The rate compares favourably with 12-month tied deposits of banks, with only the state-owned Konzumbank offering a comparable rate, for sterling from June 30 on.
CA launched its CA Foreign Currency Bond Fund in 1996, taking advantage of legal changes which opened up the Hungarian market last July 1 to state bonds issued by OECD member governments.
The law also allowed the trading of bonds and shares of firms registered in OECD countries which hold the highest rating by any of five large international credit rating agencies.
CA's Currency Bond Fund, which CA will transform into an open-ended fund from July 1, was the first in Hungary investing in foreign government securities.
"This means that this investment fund has an extremely low risk," Lantos said. "We think it carries lower risks from the investors' points of view than placing it with a bank as deposit."

The fund attempts to minimise investors' risk by focusing its investments on U.S. dollar-denominated and German government mark-denominated papers, buying in proportion to the 70 percent/30 percent mark/dollar make-up of the currency basket against which the forint floats.
"From time to time we have diverted from this proportion... but in such cases we hedge back to the 30 (percent) dollar, 70 (percent) mark," Lantos said.
